brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Built as low shelf/storage platform: 12x full hex bases (piece:12) in two levels forming flat topped surfaces, 8x solid covers on level 0 creating shelf decks (e.g. cover:-1,0,0;full;top etc.), caps and jointBolts locked. Provides ~453x310 mm and smaller flat areas suitable to stage books, but no vertical shelving boards or tall uprights — shape suggests storage/sideboard rather than enclosed shelf unit.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: Configurator checks geometry/collisions only (meshClash clear). All parts are 3D-printed plastic in user-chosen material; strength, load rating, waterproofing etc. are not modeled and cannot be verified. No material/layer specification exists to claim 50 kg capacity.

Drawer frames attempted as notch:0#-2,1#notch0 and notch:0#1,-2#notch4 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf variants) but current build contains 0 notch/drawer parts after cleanup of unsupported level-1 cells. No drawer storage is present to stage or open.

finish.summary: Low flat shelf/sideboard geometry built with covers locked and mesh clear, but load-rating cannot be verified in this plastic-print system and the two drawers requested are not present in the final build. Honest status is compromise: shape partly suggests shelf use, weight rating and drawers remain unmet.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
